claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink restrictions and be on 'right side of history': The Ukrainian president says the slowed-down internet is making it difficult to stop Russian attacks.
- Yemeni forces' retreat leaves Houthis in control of key Red Sea waterway: Saudi-backed forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the interim capital Aden.
- Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.
- Australian MP 'full of gratitude' upon leaving hospital after alleged car attack: The MP lost both of her legs after the alleged attack outside her electorate office four weeks ago.
- Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies age 80: Known as the 'Boss of Bosses', he was the head of all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s before his arrest broke up his drug organisation.
- Prince Harry praises war veterans on surprise visit to Ukraine: He has been showing support for injured veterans in Ukraine and praising the country's resilience.
- Canada bars Russia from Junior World Championships: Canada says it will not allow Russian athletes to compete in the Junior Ice Hockey World Championships because of the war in Ukraine.
- Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election: There has not been an election in Haiti since before the death of Jovenel Moise in 2021.
- South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating: Han Won-seok, 34, confessed to using a hidden camera and AI to get a near-perfect mark on the significant test.
- Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip: The Pope took to the skies before arriving in Cusco on the penultimate day of his Latin America tour.
- Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision, says NTSB: Preliminary findings by National Transportation Safety Board investigators suggest the tanker suffered a "steering casualty" before colliding with the cruise ship on Friday.
- Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media: Protesters say the move will stifle media freedom, while the government insists broadcasters need to cut costs.
